title: Identity vs. Value Ambiguity in Value Objects
pattern: Comparing Value Objects (which represent descriptive attributes with no conceptual identity) using reference/pointer comparison instead of structural equality.
why_bad: Value Objects are defined solely by their attributes, not their memory locations. Two separate allocations of the name "John Smith" are interchangeable. Checking pointer equality is a semantic defect because it reports they are unequal simply because they reside at different memory addresses.
detection: Match comparisons of structs classified as Value Objects (like `Money`, `Name`, `Color`) performed via pointer identity operators (e.g. `std::ptr::eq` or `==` on references when derived Eq is missing).
source: *Domain-Driven Design* by Eric Evans (Chapter 5, p. 83); *Domain Modeling made Functional* by Scott Wlaschin (p. 92).
